back: Analysis → objectives → strategy → implementation (marketing mix and budget decisions) → control. Resource allocation is part of it.
Marketing mix modelling · budget optimisation · sales forecasting · price optimisation.
Analyses (causal) relationships between a dependent variable (Y) and one (simple) or more (multiple) independent variables – to explain and to predict.
DV: metric (interval/ratio). IVs: metric, or nominal as dummies (k categories → k−1 dummies, baseline omitted). Ordinal: not in traditional regression.
Model formulation (theory, linearity) → estimation (OLS) → test of the function (R², adj. R², F) → test of coefficients (t-test).
Intercept b0: estimated Y when X = 0. Slope b1: change in Y for a one-unit change in X (ceteris paribus in multiple regression).
Residual = observed − estimated value. OLS chooses the parameters that minimise the sum of squared residuals.
R² = explained variance / total variance (0–1). Grows with every added IV → adjusted R² corrects for the number of IVs.
H0: βj = 0. t = b / SE. Significant if |t_emp| > t_tab or p < 0.05. Only significant coefficients are interpreted.
Different units → absolute coefficient size ≠ importance. Standardise coefficients to compare.
1 check model significance & R² · 2 mark p < 0.05 · 3 interpret sign and size of significant betas · 4 forecast = intercept + Σ significant β × value (dummies 0/1).
Statistically significant but not causal relationship explained by a third variable (ice cream sales ↔ murders, both driven by weather).
